clues.explanation: Band-Aid literally covers wounds and it's in medicine cabinets on every continent — the most helpful cover-up in history.
Mom kisses the boo-boo first, then smooths one on — the original two-step first aid protocol.
It's only rated for physical wounds; you cannot stick one on hurt feelings, though people have definitely tried.
The wound that earned it hurts, but ripping it off a week later hurts more — two pains for the price of one.

clues.text: YOU STICK WITH THEM 'CAUSE THEY'RE STUCK ON YOU
clues.explanation: The adhesive side is extremely committed and will stick with you through thick, thin, and every last arm hair.
Between the pipe and deducing a man's backstory from cigar ash, he detected more from smoke than any fire alarm ever could.

clues.text: A MAN WITH MANY BRIEF CASES
clues.explanation: Cases that are brief AND the kind you carry — this man was basically built for a good double meaning.

clues.text: JUST LIKE YOU, HE LOVES A GOOD CLUE
clues.explanation: He built his entire career on following them, cataloguing them, and annoying Watson with them — sound familiar?

clues.text: SCHOOLS HIS DEAR SIDEKICK IN THE WAYS OF INVESTIGATION
clues.explanation: 'Elementary, my dear Watson' was basically 'let me explain this very slowly, again.'

clues.text: FICTIONAL BRITISH SLEUTH WHO ALWAYS FINDS THE TRUTH
clues.explanation: 221B Baker Street, pipe, deerstalker, and a perfect solve rate — the one and only.
Invented in 1904 — Ohio and Pennsylvania are still arguing about who did it first, but America has claimed this dessert for over 120 years and is not letting go.
The ice cream melts and the banana softens, so this dessert comes with a built-in deadline — order it fast.
The long oval dish it's served in is literally called a boat, which makes every banana split a tiny dessert voyage.
The banana brings the peel; the dessert brings the appeal — one letter, maximum pun, zero apologies.

clues.text: PEOPLE GO NUTS FOR ITS 3 SCOOPS
clues.explanation: Three scoops of ice cream, whipped cream, a cherry on top, and yes — actual nuts, so the clue was being completely literal the whole time.
Manhattan and Staten Island say hello — NYC is literally built on islands, yet somehow still the most landlocked-feeling place on Earth traffic-wise.
The City That Never Sleeps — it's a point of pride, not a diagnosis, and the 24-hour deli scene is not helping anyone wind down.

clues.text: THAT IS ONE GIANT PIECE OF FRUIT
clues.explanation: The Big Apple — nobody is entirely sure how the nickname started, but jazz musicians, horse racing, and a 1970s tourism campaign all take partial credit.

clues.text: DESPITE ITS NAME, IT'S OVER 200 YEARS OLD
clues.explanation: 'New' York was founded as New Amsterdam in 1624 and renamed in 1664 — four centuries old and still calling itself new, which is frankly iconic.

clues.text: IT'S SO NICE THEY NAMED IT TWICE
clues.explanation: The state and the city share the name, Frank Sinatra made a whole song about saying it twice, and if you can make it there you can make it anywhere.
